svg.aria-label: Fig 4. Planned voice agent. A browser call links on a blue two-way line to our own mock payer rep, and black tracks take the rep audio to local speech-to-text, the text to the agent turn (Muse, AI disclosed) and the reply to local text-to-speech. A dashed track takes the spoken reply back into the call, and a green track takes the result to a call outcome card with the synthetic reference SYN-REF-0007.
svg.title: Fig 4. Planned voice agent. A browser call links on a blue two-way line to our own mock payer rep, and black tracks take the rep audio to local speech-to-text, the text to the agent turn (Muse, AI disclosed) and the reply to local text-to-speech. A dashed track takes the spoken reply back into the call, and a green track takes the result to a call outcome card with the synthetic reference SYN-REF-0007.
svg.text: Free tools only. No phone line. No real payer. Planned design, not built.
calls go only to our own mock
1 The call runs in the browser (WebRTC and Web Audio). There is no paid phone line.
2 Local speech-to-text turns the rep's voice into text. Candidates: Whisper or faster-whisper.
3 The agent picks the next turn with Muse. It says that it is an AI and announces the recording.
4 Local text-to-speech speaks the agent's turn. Candidates: Piper or Kokoro.
Each voice model gets a license check. Non-commercial voices are not allowed (D-018).
5 The rep is our own mock payer rep on the payer mock. Never call a real payer.
6 The agent records the rep name, the reference number and the time, and reads them back.
The call outcome updates the claim in the review console.
blue: the two-way call line between 1 and 5. The voice of the rep comes in on this line.
black: the audio of the rep goes from 1 to 2, the text to 3 and the reply to 4.
dashed: the spoken reply goes from 4 back into the call. green: the call result goes to 6.
